mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary stance that raises discount rates and depresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when the trigger is met, or the trigger fails to predict direction in at least three consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate below 3.5% for three consecutive months indicates an overheating labor market, which increases wage pressures and inflation expectations, ultimately resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as profit margins are squeezed.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the trigger is not followed by CPI acceleration.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent and sustained decline in both personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) for two consecutive quarters signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or GDP and housing do not continue to decline after the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals supply-side weakness, which raises input costs and reduces profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month moving average for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered instances, or industrial production rebounds within two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month decline in the federal funds rate below 3% during a recession signals aggressive monetary easing, which supports risk assets and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS drops below 3% in one month during recession (UNRATE > 6%)
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered recession episodes, or the rate cut is not followed by economic recovery signals.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both unemployment rate (UNRATE) and payroll employment (PAYEMS) month-over-month is contradictory and signals a data anomaly or temporary statistical noise, which historically has preceded short-term S&P 500 volatility and negative 5-day returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases while PAYEMS also increases in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 70% of such anomalous months, or the pattern ceases to predict returns after a policy regime change.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 5-year average for six consecutive months, coupled with a flat GDP (GDPC1), indicates pent-up household savings and weak consumption, which typically precedes a delayed but persistent equity drawdown over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 5-year average for six months AND GDPC1 flat (change < 0.2% q/q)
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or savings do not remain elevated after the trigger window.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent divergence between industrial production (INDPRO) and the S&P 500 index over three months, where INDPRO falls while the S&P 500 rises, signals a decoupling of economic activity from equity valuations driven by speculative factors; this pattern tends to reverse within 20 trading days with negative equity returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines for three months while S&P 500 rises (proxy: use only INDPRO as available proxy)
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns remain positive in more than 60% of such decoupling episodes, or the pattern fails to recur in subsequent years.
